headline: Homebuilders Lead a Broadly Positive Thursday as Networking Names Diverge Sharply
body_html:
Midway through Thursday's session, the tape is tilting comfortably to the upside: 367 names in our universe are trading higher against 177 in the red, a breadth reading that points to genuine participation rather than index-level noise. Homebuilders are the clear sector pacesetter, up roughly a full percentage point, while Software, Materials, and Semiconductors are each adding between half a point and two-thirds of a point. Energy is the lone sector in negative territory, off 0.14%, as geopolitical cross-currents around the Strait of Hormuz keep crude-demand assumptions fluid.

The standout mover of the session is Harmonic (HLIT), surging more than 20% and drawing attention to the Tech-Networking space. That enthusiasm has not spread evenly, however — Cisco (CSCO) is simultaneously down nearly 9%, a divergence that underscores how sharply investors are differentiating within the same broad category. EnerSys (ENS) is the second-biggest gainer, up 15%, lending further lift to the Industrials tape.

On the downside, Tapestry (TPR) is off more than 15%, leading a weak showing from consumer-brand names including YETI Holdings, down nearly 11%. Into the close, traders will be watching Treasury markets closely — yields are dipping as participants position ahead of wholesale inflation data, a release that could reprice rate expectations and reset the session's narrative quickly.

briefs.headline: Harmonic Surges 20% on Midday Tape, Dominating Tech-Networking Conversation
briefs.body: Harmonic (HLIT) is the session's most dramatic mover, adding more than a fifth of its value in intraday trading. The Tech-Networking name has drawn heavy volume and is pulling attention from the broader connectivity space, even as neighboring names move in the opposite direction.

briefs.headline: Cisco Drops Nearly 9%, Creating a Stark Split Inside Networking Sector
briefs.body: Cisco (CSCO) is nursing a loss approaching 9% — a rare single-session decline for one of networking's marquee names. The contrast with Harmonic's simultaneous rally highlights the granular, name-by-name nature of today's tape rather than any broad sector-wide theme.

briefs.headline: Tapestry Leads Consumer Decliners with a 15% Midday Drop
briefs.body: Tapestry (TPR) is the session's largest loser among consumer names, falling more than 15% as midday trading approaches. YETI Holdings is also under heavy pressure, off nearly 11%, suggesting selective but meaningful selling pressure across consumer-brand equities.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Ease as Wholesale Inflation Data Looms Over Afternoon Trade
briefs.body: Government bond yields are drifting lower Thursday as market participants take a cautious stance ahead of a closely watched wholesale inflation print. The data release has the potential to shift rate-path expectations and inject fresh volatility into the final hours of the session.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Standoff Adds Uncertainty to Energy Sector, Which Lags the Tape
briefs.body: Competing claims between Iran and the United States over control of the Strait of Hormuz are casting a shadow over the Energy sector, which is the only group in the red at midday. Reuters reported separately that analysts are weighing whether global oil stockpiles are sufficient to absorb a prolonged period of US-Iran hostilities.

briefs.headline: Diesel Prices Climb Above Jet Fuel in Europe as Supply Strains Spread
briefs.body: European diesel prices have overtaken jet-fuel costs as a widening global supply shortage reshapes regional energy markets, according to Reuters. The dynamic adds another layer of complexity to commodity positioning at a moment when Middle East tensions are already keeping traders on edge.
